Invariant: After any Deposit by an account and a subsequent Collect by that same account, the balances mapping entry for that account decreases by the collected amount (i.e., Collect reduces caller's balances[msg.sender] by _am when successful); the mutant breaks this because Deposit credited address(0) instead of the depositor so Collect can succeed on the reference but leave the caller's balance unchanged in the mutant, producing differing balances at some key.

For every depositor and amount, if Collect succeeds then the depositor's balance after Collect equals their prior balance minus the collected amount (the reference always deducts from the caller's balances key; the mutant sometimes credited address(0) on Deposit so Collect can succeed but leaves caller's balances unchanged, producing a differing balances entry).

For any depositor address A, if A previously made a Deposit of some value and then successfully calls Collect(x) that transfers x out, then the total sum of all balances stored in the mapping (sum over all addresses accessible through the public getter) decreases by exactly x in the reference, but the mutant (which credited address(0) on Deposit) can leave the caller's own balance unchanged while decreasing the overall stored sum at a different key; thus the reference preserves total stored-sum change == -x on successful Collect, the mutant can violate it.

For any depositor and any collect amount, if Collect succeeds then the caller's balance after Collect equals its balance before Collect minus the collected amount; the mutant can break this because Deposit increments balances[address(0)] instead of balances[msg.sender], so Collect can succeed while the caller's own balance is unchanged.

For any caller who successfully Collects, the reference contract always reduces some mapping entry's value by the collected amount at the caller's own balances key (balances[caller] decreases by _am); the mutant that credited balances[address(0)] during Deposit can cause Collect to succeed while the caller's balances entry does not decrease, violating that invariant.

property_summary: Calling SetLogFile(...) never reverts (i.e., it always completes) for any address input in the original contract.

Invariant: once Initialized() has NOT been called, calling SetLogFile on the reference C only succeeds when initialization flag is false (i.e., after calling Initialized() the Log cannot be changed) — the mutant removes the guard so SetLogFile can change Log after initialization, violating that invariant.

For any caller address passed to SetLogFile, the reference contract C sets its Log state to that passed address (cast to LogFile) — the mutant instead always sets Log to address(0), breaking this property for some inputs.

For any address input, the reference C stores that address (cast to LogFile) into its public Log state variable when SetLogFile is called (unless already initialized), whereas the mutant always sets Log to the zero address, so there exist inputs where C.Log() != address(0) but the mutant would be address(0).
